title: Pizza ai Frutti di Mare
subtitle: Pizza with mixed seafood, tomato, garlic, and parsley: no mozzarella
excerpt: Pizza ai frutti di mare is a seafood pizza with no mozzarella: prawns, clams, mussels, and squid on a tomato base with garlic, parsley, and chilli. The Italian rule for seafood pizza is no cheese, which keeps the seafood flavour clean and prevents the mozzarella from competing with or masking the brininess of the shellfish.
sourceNotes: Pizza ai frutti di mare is a Neapolitan and southern Italian pizza tradition. The no-cheese rule for seafood pizza is a firmly held Italian culinary convention, reflecting the same principle that keeps cheese off pasta alle vongole: the seafood flavour must not be competed with.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Dough can be cold-proved 24 to 48 hours. Prep seafood day-of.
recipe.temperatureNote: maximum oven temperature, pizza stone or steel

content.text: The Italian rule about seafood pizza is absolute: no cheese. Adding mozzarella to a seafood pizza kills the delicate brininess of the shellfish and creates a heavy, muddy result. The pizza is instead flavoured with garlic, parsley, chilli, and olive oil over the tomato base. The seafood: prawns, clams, mussels, squid: goes on in the last 5 minutes of baking so it does not overcook.

items.prepNote: cleaned, cooked and shelled (or use frozen)

content.text: Make the dough (flour, water, yeast, salt, olive oil), knead 8 to 10 minutes, divide into 4 balls, and cold-prove 24 to 48 hours. Preheat pizza stone at 250°C fan for 45 to 60 minutes.

Roll or stretch each dough ball to a 28 to 30 cm round. Transfer to baking paper. Spread a thin layer of seasoned tomato sauce with the sliced garlic scattered over it. No mozzarella. Drizzle with olive oil and add chilli flakes if using.

Slide the pizza onto the hot stone and bake for 4 to 5 minutes until the base begins to set and colour. Slide out, add the seafood (prawns, squid, mussels) quickly, drizzle with more olive oil, and return to the oven for 4 to 5 more minutes until the seafood is just cooked and the base is crisp.
Scatter with chopped parsley immediately on removing from the oven. Serve at once: seafood pizza waits for no one.

items.cause: Seafood was added from the beginning and cooked the full baking time
items.fix: Always use the two-stage bake: base first for 4 to 5 minutes, then seafood added and baked for only 4 to 5 more minutes. Prawns and squid particularly overcook very quickly.

items.symptom: Pizza tastes fishy rather than briny
items.cause: Seafood was not fresh or was not properly prepped
items.fix: Use very fresh seafood and dry it thoroughly before placing on the pizza. Excess moisture and pre-cooked seafood can both cause a strong fishy rather than briny taste.

items.symptom: Base is wet under the seafood
items.cause: Seafood released water during the short bake
items.fix: Pat all seafood dry before topping. Pre-cook mussels and clams just until they open; drain very thoroughly before using.

content.text: Pizza ai frutti di mare is based on the Italian rule that fish and cheese do not go together. This is a firm belief in Italian coastal cooking, not just a convention. The pizza comes from the southern Italian coast, in particular Naples and the Campanian coastline.
